definitions.explanation: The process of adapting a novel, manga, or other source material into a television drama series. A common practice in Japanese entertainment.

examples.japanese: あの{小説|しょうせつ}がドラマ{化|か}された。
examples.english: That novel was adapted into a TV drama.

examples.japanese: {人気|にんき}マンガのドラマ{化|か}が{決定|けってい}した。
examples.english: It was decided that the popular manga will be adapted into a drama.

examples.japanese: ドラマ{化|か}にあたって、{原作|げんさく}のストーリーが{大|おお}きく{変|か}わることもある。
examples.english: When adapting into a drama, the original story sometimes changes significantly.

notes:
A compound of ドラマ (drama, i.e., TV drama series) + {化|か} (transformation, -ization). In Japan, adapting manga and novels into live-action TV dramas is extremely common and often generates significant buzz. The suffix {化|か} is productive and attaches to many nouns to mean 'turning into X.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ドラマ{化|か}される: to be adapted into a drama (passive)
- ドラマ{化|か}が{決定|けってい}: drama adaptation confirmed
- ドラマ{化|か}にあたって: in adapting into a drama
- {実写|じっしゃ}ドラマ{化|か}: live-action drama adaptation

SIMILAR PATTERNS:
- {映画化|えいがか}: film adaptation
- {アニメ化|あにめか}: anime adaptation
- {舞台化|ぶたいか}: stage adaptation
- {漫画化|まんがか}: manga adaptation (reverse direction)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese TV dramas (typically 10-12 episodes per season) are a major entertainment format. Successful adaptations of manga and novels often boost sales of the original work dramatically.
